narrative.overview:
Hoisted looks like the inside of a JavaScript runtime, seen by someone who finally understands it. Surfaces are deep night ink, layered in quiet tonal steps. The JS yellow is the signal, the way a cursor or a breakpoint is: small, exact, and always meaning "here". Code, terminal prompts, `//` comments and `~/path` breadcrumbs are the material of the brand, never pasted on as decoration. Every screen should feel like a well-made developer tool before it feels like a marketing page.

Density follows the surface. Public pages breathe (56px between sections, generous gutters, one large display headline). The console areas for admins and instructors are compact and scannable: 13px body, mono labels, tables and list rows. Both share one token set and one component vocabulary, so a learner moving into the instructor studio recognises it immediately.

Precision beats ornament. Depth comes from tonal layering and hairlines, not stacked shadows. Emphasis comes from weight and the single accent, not gradients. Motion is one authored entrance (the reveal) plus the living details of a terminal (blinking caret, scrolling ticker), and it all switches off under reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first: dark is the default theme. Light mode is a real theme, not an inversion, and it swaps the accent from JS yellow to indigo for contrast.
One accent at a time, carried by the semantic `accent` token.
Two typefaces: Inter Tight for language, JetBrains Mono for anything a machine would print.
Flat by default, tonal layers, 1px hairlines at 9–10% opacity (`--line` is an RGB triplet, `--line-a` its strength).
Always-dark code surfaces, in both themes.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: The accent marks exactly what the user should act on or where they are: one primary button per view, the active nav item, focus, progress. If two things on a screen glow yellow, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Token-Not-Hex Rule
rules.body: Themed surfaces use the semantic tokens (`bg`, `bg-1…3`, `ink`, `ink-2…3`, `line`, `accent`, `accent-ink`) through Tailwind, never raw hex. The raw `js` yellow is reserved for always-dark surfaces such as auth side panels and code windows, where the theme never changes.

rules.name: The Status Is Not Brand Rule
rules.body: Green, rose and amber appear only when they report a state. Never use them to decorate a card, colour a category, or add variety.

rules.name: The Machine Truth Rule
rules.body: If a computer would print it (a price, a count, an ID, a path, code, a timestamp), set it in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals. Sentences meant for people are never mono.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Gradient Rule
rules.body: Emphasis inside a headline comes from the accent colour on one phrase, or from weight. Gradient text (`bg-clip-text`) is not part of this system.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow means "this is above the page" (overlay) or "act here" (signal glow). A card at rest never carries a shadow.

rules.name: The Always-Dark Code Rule
rules.body: Code windows, IDE frames and terminal blocks stay dark (`#0d1117` / Ink Night) in both themes, with their own syntax palette. They are the one place a fixed palette overrides theming.

dos: Do let section headings stand alone. No numbered kickers ("01 / Chủ đề") or `//` labels above a heading; the `~/hoisted / path` breadcrumb is the only line allowed above an H1, because it tells the user where they are.
Do show a number only when it is real and non-zero; hide the stat, the category or the testimonial block instead of printing "0" or a one-word review.
Do use the semantic tokens (`bg-bg-1`, `text-ink-2`, `border-line`, `bg-accent text-accent-ink`) for every themed surface, so light mode swaps correctly.
Do keep one primary (accent) button per view, with the Signal Glow only on the page's main call to action.
Do set prices, counts, codes, durations and paths in JetBrains Mono with `tabular-nums`.
Do separate surfaces with tone and 1px hairlines before reaching for a shadow.
Do give every icon-only control an `aria-label`, and keep a visible focus state.
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion`: the reveal, marquee, float and caret all stop.
donts: Don't use gradient text (`bg-clip-text` with a gradient) for emphasis. Use the accent on one phrase, or weight.
Don't use purple or violet as a decorative accent or gradient. The difficulty scale uses Pass Green → JS Yellow → Fail Rose.
Don't hardcode `#F7DF1E` or any hex on a themed surface. Use `accent`, which is indigo in light mode.
Don't use status colours (green, rose, amber) to decorate. They only report state.
Don't give resting cards a shadow, or stack shadow on shadow.
Don't use `warning` colour classes. The token is `warn`, and `bg-warning` generates nothing.
Don't use emoji or unicode glyphs as icons in new UI. Use lucide-react at 14–20px with a consistent stroke.
